newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso grants Americel B Band concession.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso grants Americel B Band concession.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has formally granted a Canadian-led group the concession to operate B Band cellular services in central and western Brazil, including the capital, an official decree said.
Cardoso's office issued a decree late Tuesday granting Americel S.A., led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada and Telesystem, also of Canada, the license to operate in B Band area 7.
Americel was the lone bidder last week for the largely rural area covering Acre, Goias, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Rondonia and Tocantins states and the federal district of Brasilia.
The group, which also includes Citibank, local bank Opportunity and pension funds owned by Banco do Brasil, offered 338.5 million reais, some 25.4 percent above the base price.
The bid was opened and the offer accepted last Wednesday by the Communications Ministry's privatization committee.
Eight of nine other B Band concessions across the country are slated to be granted in the coming weeks.
Still to come are the coveted areas of Sao Paulo city and state, Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states and Minas Gerais state, hotly contested areas where experts predict large premiums.

The panel last week announced that 10 of 15 groups who presented proposals in early April qualified for the tenders. Disqualified groups have until 1700 local/2000 gmt today (Wednesday) to appeal against the committee's decisions.
At least one consortium, Tess, was expected to present an appeal. If that happens, the government has 20 days to rebut the group's arguments.
